units.title: Unit 79 — Phrasal verbs 1: form and meaning
units.source: Vocabulary study targets from published reference material; Unit 79. Page information, if available, is retained in sourceAudit.
learningObjectives: Recognise common two-part and three-part phrasal verbs in context.
Distinguish literal and idiomatic meanings, including when a particle adds a new meaning.
Use common verb-particle combinations related to movement, possession, work, and daily life.
Interpret multiple meanings of go off, pick up, put on, and go away.
Choose the appropriate particle and meaning in original example sentences.

items.example: He fell over while running across the park.
items.note: Intransitive in this sense; past tense: fell over.

items.example: We need to find out why the train is late.
items.note: Often followed by a question clause: find out why. A noun object can also follow it: find out the answer.

items.example: I gave my old books away last weekend.
items.note: Separable: give them away, not give away them.

items.example: Look the expression up in a dictionary.
items.note: Separable: look it up. This is different from physically looking upwards.

items.example: We sorted the booking problem out yesterday.
items.note: Separable: sort it out, not sort out it.

items.example: She gets on well with her neighbours.
items.note: Three-part verb; the person follows with. The adverb well can follow on.

items.example: I woke up much earlier than usual.
items.note: The particle up is optional in many contexts: I woke at six.

items.example: We are saving up for a new washing machine.
items.note: Usually refers to saving money for a future purchase; save without up is also possible.

items.example: Hurry up, or the bus will leave without us.
items.note: The particle up can be omitted in some uses.

items.example: I need to lie down after the long journey.
items.note: Intransitive; lie, lay, lain, when referring to reclining.

items.example: She took the damaged kettle back to the shop.
items.note: Often means return something to its previous location or the seller.

items.pt: colocar algo de volta no lugar
items.example: Put the folder back on the shelf when you finish.
items.note: Separable: put it back.

items.example: They plan to go back to Edinburgh in September.
items.note: Back adds the meaning of returning to a previous place.

items.example: He gave up drinking fizzy drinks.
items.note: Give up + -ing can mean stop doing an activity.

items.example: After a short break, we carried on working.
items.note: Follow with an -ing form or with + noun.

items.example: The shop put up its prices this month.
items.note: Put up can mean increase an amount; this verb is separable.

items.example: The company will take on extra staff in spring.
items.note: Take on here means employ; separable when a specific object is used.

items.example: The visitors went away after the meeting.
items.note: Meaning: leave a place; different from go away on holiday.

items.example: We usually go away for a few days in August.
items.note: Meaning: leave home for a short trip or holiday.

items.example: He picked his keys up from the carpet.
items.note: Lift or collect an object; separable: pick it up.

items.pt: buscar alguém; dar carona a alguém
items.example: Could you pick our guests up at the airport?
items.note: Collect someone, often in a vehicle; separable: pick her up.

items.example: Please put the hall light on before going downstairs.
items.note: Switch on electrical equipment; put it on is separable.

items.pt: vestir uma roupa; colocar uma peça de roupa
items.example: She put her warm coat on before leaving.
items.note: Put on means dress in an item of clothing; separable: put it on.

items.example: Switch the radio on when the programme starts.
items.note: An alternative to put on or turn on for electrical equipment.

items.example: The heating goes off automatically at midnight.
items.note: Used when a light, heater, or machine stops operating.

items.example: My alarm went off before sunrise.
items.note: An alarm or other device suddenly makes a noise.

items.example: The milk has gone off, so do not drink it.
items.note: British English: food becomes too old to eat safely.

items.example: A firework went off in the distance.
items.note: Used for an explosion or a gun firing.

items.example: He went off to visit his sister.
items.note: The person leaves to go somewhere else.

units.title: Unit 80 — Phrasal verbs 2: grammar and style
units.source: Vocabulary study targets from published reference material; Unit 80. Page information, if available, is retained in sourceAudit.
learningObjectives: Recognise phrasal verbs that do not take an object.
Place noun objects and pronoun objects correctly in separable phrasal verbs.
Identify phrasal verbs whose objects cannot separate the verb and particle.
Use grammar patterns from dictionary entries to interpret phrasal verbs.
Distinguish informal phrasal verbs from their more formal single-word counterparts.

items.pt: verbo frasal intransitivo; sem objeto direto
items.example: The train got in late, but everyone was safe.
items.note: A phrasal verb that does not take a direct object; nothing can be inserted between its parts.

items.example: Our train gets in just after nine.
items.note: Intransitive: arrive, especially for transport.

items.example: Hold on while I check the address.
items.note: An informal request to wait; often used in conversation.

items.example: Our car broke down on the motorway.
items.note: Intransitive here: a machine or vehicle stops working.

items.example: I will call for you at the hotel entrance.
items.note: Call for someone means go to their location to collect them; the person follows for.

items.example: We set off before the roads became busy.
items.note: Intransitive when it means begin a journey.

items.example: She put her gloves on at the door.
items.note: With a noun object, both positions often work; a long noun phrase usually follows the particle. Pronouns go in the middle.

items.pt: vestir; colocar uma peça de roupa
items.example: He put on a jumper because it was cold.
items.note: Put on the jumper / put the jumper on; with it, say put it on.

items.example: Please turn the fan on for a few minutes.
items.note: Turn on the fan / turn the fan on; with it, say turn it on.

items.pt: tirar; remover uma peça de roupa
items.example: Take your muddy boots off at the door.
items.note: Take off your boots / take your boots off; with them, say take them off.

items.example: Turn the kitchen light off before you leave.
items.note: Use turn it off, not turn off it.

items.example: This scarf is warm; put it on.
items.note: With separable phrasal verbs, a direct-object pronoun must occur between the verb and particle.

items.example: Your shoes are wet; take them off.
items.note: Correct: take them off. Incorrect: take off them.

items.example: The documents are ready; hand them out now.
items.note: Correct: hand them out. Incorrect: hand out them.

items.example: She looks after her little brother at weekends.
items.note: An object must follow the entire phrasal verb, even when it is a pronoun.

items.example: He looks after his niece on Fridays.
items.note: Not separable: look after her, not look her after.

items.example: Someone tried to break into the office overnight.
items.note: Not separable: break into a building, not break a building into.

items.pt: ficar à toa; permanecer sem fazer muito
items.example: Several people were hanging around outside the station.
items.note: Intransitive; do not insert a place between hang and around.

items.pt: ficar à toa; permanecer sem fazer muito
items.example: They were hanging about near the entrance.
items.note: British English alternative to hang around.

items.example: The volunteers handed leaflets out at the event.
items.note: Separable: hand out the leaflets / hand the leaflets out; hand them out.

items.example: It took her a week to get over the illness.
items.note: Not separable: get over it, not get it over in this sense.

items.example: The organisers left three names out of the programme.
items.note: Separable: leave me out. Formal alternative in some contexts: omit.

items.example: He made up an excuse for arriving late.
items.note: Meaning: invent; often informal. Separable: make it up.

items.example: We put the appointment off until next Tuesday.
items.note: Separable: put it off. More formal synonym: postpone.

items.example: She turned the job offer down after the interview.
items.note: Separable: turn it down. More formal synonym: reject.

items.example: Please omit the final paragraph from the summary.
items.note: More formal alternative to leave out in this meaning.

items.example: The writer invented a new character for the story.
items.note: More formal alternative to make up in this meaning.

items.example: They decided to postpone the workshop.
items.note: More formal alternative to put off.

items.example: The committee rejected the proposal.
items.note: More formal alternative to turn down.
